label: Riemann-Roch for Cauchy-Riemann Operators
notes: Appendix C supplies the index bookkeeping behind every moduli dimension in the book. A real-linear Cauchy-Riemann operator on a bundle over a closed Riemann surface is Fredholm, and its index is fixed entirely by topology: the rank, the genus through the Euler characteristic, and the first Chern number of the bundle.

label: The Cauchy-Riemann Operator Setup
notes: We work with a complex bundle E over a closed Riemann surface and a real-linear operator that differs from a complex-linear dbar by a zeroth-order term. The lower-order term does not change the index, so the analytic problem reduces to a model whose Fredholm theory is controlled by elliptic estimates on Sobolev completions.

label: The Real Index Formula
notes: The central identity states that the real index equals n times the Euler characteristic plus twice the pairing of the first Chern class with the fundamental class. Equivalently it is two times n times one minus g plus the degree. Degree raises the index by two; each handle lowers it by two.

label: Classical Holomorphic Riemann-Roch
notes: For a holomorphic line bundle L the kernel and cokernel become the sheaf cohomology groups H zero and H one. Their dimensions difference equals degree plus one minus genus. This is the form learned in algebraic geometry, and it specializes the analytic statement when the operator is honestly complex-linear and integrable.

label: Serre Duality and the Cokernel
notes: Serre duality identifies the cokernel of the operator on L with the kernel of the dual problem on the canonical bundle twisted by L inverse. This turns obstruction counting into a second section count, makes the index formula symmetric, and explains why the canonical bundle of degree two g minus two governs vanishing thresholds.

label: Kernel Versus Cokernel Tradeoff
notes: The index is a stable difference even though kernel and cokernel dimensions jump. As degree increases past two g minus two the cokernel vanishes and the kernel grows linearly. Holomorphic sections, the kernel, trade against obstructions, the cokernel, while their signed difference stays pinned by topology.

label: A Genus-g Surface and Sections
notes: Visualizing a genus g surface carrying a degree d line bundle makes the section count tangible. For large degree the space of holomorphic sections has dimension d plus one minus g, the obstruction space is empty, and the moduli model is unobstructed. Lowering degree reintroduces cohomology in degree one.

label: The Determinant Line Bundle
notes: For a family of Cauchy-Riemann operators the kernels and cokernels may jump, but the top exterior power of the kernel tensored with the dual top power of the cokernel patches into a smooth determinant line over the parameter space. Its orientability underwrites coherent orientations of moduli spaces.

label: Linearization and Virtual Dimension
notes: Linearizing the dbar equation at a J-holomorphic curve u gives a Cauchy-Riemann operator on the pullback bundle u star T M. Riemann-Roch computes its index, which is the expected or virtual dimension of the moduli space. With n now half the real dimension of the target, the formula reads two n one minus g plus two c one.

label: Boundary Problems and the Maslov Index
notes: When the surface has boundary mapped into a Lagrangian, totally real boundary conditions add a Maslov term. In the disk model one full rotation of the boundary line contributes Maslov index two, and the index becomes rank plus Maslov, generalizing the closed formula to bordered curves used in Floer theory.

label: Gluing and Index Additivity
notes: Gluing two curves at a node is index bookkeeping: the glued index equals the sum of the piece indices minus the real dimension of the matching constraint at the node. This additivity, together with disk base cases and elliptic estimates, is exactly how the appendix assembles the general Riemann-Roch theorem.

label: Recap: The Index Toolkit
notes: Riemann-Roch converts an analytic Fredholm index into rank, Euler characteristic, and Chern number. Serre duality balances kernel against cokernel, the determinant line orients families, and the linearized operator on u star T M delivers virtual dimensions. Compute the index panel first, then ask for transversality and compactness.
